title: Polynomial Order Chooser
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Robot Motion Planning
description: Compare a cubic, a quintic and a cubic spline: what each can control, and what the position and the acceleration of an example move look like. Then decide which kind each of eight trajectory requirements needs. Used in Chapter 19.

educational.topic: Choosing a cubic, a quintic or a cubic spline trajectory from its boundary conditions
learningObjectives: Differentiate eight trajectory requirements as needing a cubic, a quintic or a cubic spline, with at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Compare the three kinds by what they control and how their acceleration looks, then separate similar-looking requirements by counting conditions
keyQuestions: How many conditions does each requirement state?
What can a quintic control that a cubic cannot?
commonMisconceptions: A higher degree is always smoother
One polynomial can pass through any number of via points well
A cubic can keep the acceleration continuous with the last move
assessmentOpportunities: Eight committed choices, one attempt each; 7 of 8 for mastery
